nb.parts.intro: Write these in a class and save: every creature of that class morphs at once. Click to preview. 🔒 parts need Crystal research first.
nb.resources.body:
✦ Essence: creatures gather it from the floor (it bubbles up around the well). eat() it, spend it on new creatures, and upgrade machines with it (click a machine in the lab). An upgraded well grows golden Essence: worth 5, gone in 15 s.

⚡ Mana: the whole lab's command budget per tick. Every move / eat / gather costs 1; when it runs out, some creatures skip that tick. Lean code feeds more creatures. Upgrade the generator for more Mana and faster fast-forward.

◆ Crystal: earned from orders, spent on research for new parts (Parts page).
nb.locked: 🔒 This page opens with the quest "{quest}".
nb.lesson.if.title: if: let the creature decide
nb.lesson.if.body:
Day 3: my slime gathered until it fainted from hunger. It only does what I say.
if (condition) { … } runs only when the condition is true; else { … } is the other way.
Now it knows to eat when it's hungry.
nb.lesson.loop.title: loops: say it once, repeat it
nb.lesson.loop.body:
I wrote gather 10 times until my hand hurt.
while (condition) { … } repeats while the condition is true.
for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) { … } repeats a number of times.
Careful: a loop that never ends makes the creature dizzy.
nb.lesson.function.title: functions: give steps a name
nb.lesson.function.body:
The same steps kept showing up all over my notes, so I named them.
function gatherThree() { … }, then call gatherThree() anywhere, as often as you like.
Fix it once and every call is fixed.
nb.lesson.class.title: class and new: a creature mould
nb.lesson.class.body:
Ordering 10 slimes one by one? Never again.
A class is a mould; new Slime() stamps out a new one (written outside the class).

update() is its brain: the game calls every creature's update() for you, every tick (10 times a second), and each time it picks one thing to do.
Inside a class you write if, loops and variables as before, but a creature calls itself this instead of slime.
nb.lesson.extends.title: extends: children get everything
nb.lesson.extends.body:
I wanted a fire slime without rewriting Slime from scratch.
class FireSlime extends Slime { … } gets everything from Slime and changes only what you write.
Change the parent and the whole family changes (what a child adds itself glows).
quest.eachOwnHunger.title: Make each slime eat by its own hunger
quest.eachOwnHunger.hint: in update(): if (this.hunger > 50) { this.eat() } else { this.gatherNearest() }
quest.eachOwnHunger.nudge: this is the creature that is thinking right now, so this.hunger is its own hunger, not anyone else's.
quest.needs.this: They're eating! But each one should check its own hunger with this.hunger.
nb.newPage: New notebook page: {title} (open the DNA machine → Lessons)
nb.lesson.this.title: this: the creature itself
nb.lesson.this.body:
10 slimes share one class, so how do they think differently?
While Mochi's update() runs, this is Mochi; while Bloop's runs, this is Bloop.
So this.hunger is the hunger of whoever is thinking: hungry ones eat, full ones go back to work.
Without this, they'd all look at the same value and eat at the same time.

ref.tdz: Line {line}: {ident} is used before class {ident} is written. Code runs top to bottom: move class {ident} above the line that calls new.
ref.syn.1002: Line {line}: a quote is never closed. Text needs " at both ends, like "Mochi".
ref.syn.1005: Line {line}: {tok} is missing here. Every bracket you open needs its pair: ( with ) and { with }.
ref.syn.1003: Line {line}: a name goes here, like a class name or a variable name.
ref.syn.1068: Line {line}: inside a class you can only write values (body = "blob") and methods (update() { … }). Other code goes inside a method.
ref.syn.1109: Line {line}: a value goes here, like a number or a name, but it's empty.
ref.syn.1127: Line {line}: a strange character. If it's a curly quote “ ”, use " instead.
ref.syn.1128: Line {line}: something extra here, maybe one } too many. Count your braces: opens and closes should match.
ref.syn.1161: Line {line}: a lone / here. For a note, use two: //
ref.syn.1434: Line {line}: an unknown word. A typo, or a missing . or ( ) between words?
